I am an old woman, and this small plot near our compound is where I plant my beans with a little maize and sorghum mixed in, like my mother taught me. I cannot afford much chemical fertilizer for beans — beans make their own strength in the soil — but I will put the manure from our goats and chickens on it before the rains. I keep the seeds from last year's harvest because they grow well here and the market seeds are too costly. My daughters-in-law and I will do most of the work ourselves, but for weeding when the rains come heavy, I will call two young men from the village for a few days.
